author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Cranston police arrested two New York men early Friday after officers recovered about 100 gallons of used cooking oil that authorities say had been taken from a local restaurant. Anyeson Veras Martinez, 26, and Steven Velez Toribio, 29, were each charged with larceny under $1,500.

Police said a Flock license-plate reader alerted officers at 1:57 a.m. to a white 2018 Ford Transit with a Pennsylvania plate associated with cooking-oil thefts. A second alert placed the van near Route 37. An officer located it at PJ's Pub on Pontiac Avenue and stopped it at about 2:20 a.m.

According to police, the van smelled of cooking oil and contained residue, two large containers, a hose and a pump. Investigators estimated the recovered oil's value at about $200. Used restaurant oil can be processed into biofuel and other products, giving it a resale value that has made storage tanks a theft target. The charges are allegations, and both men are presumed innocent unless proven guilty. Police did not immediately say whether the case is connected to other reported thefts.
dek: A license-plate reader alert led officers to a van carrying about 100 gallons of used restaurant oil, police said.
headline: Two men charged after Cranston cooking-oil theft
